item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is materially closer to the frozen contract: it adds the exact Upload API, validates inputs, uses multipartbody.NewFile, and routes the result through FilesService.Add. A changes Add semantics and bypasses it from Upload, directly contradicting two explicit requirements.","reasons":["B preserves FilesService.Add and calls it from Upload, retaining the established option, request, decoding, and error path.","B performs explicit empty-filename and nil-content validation before encoding or requesting.","A makes Add eagerly read and buffer every custom body, changing the lower-level API's existing streaming behavior and memory characteristics despite the preservation requirement.","A's Upload calls a new private add method instead of the required existing Add method, creating duplicate routing machinery and weakening the intended single path of behavior ownership."],"risks_a":["Upload lacks visible explicit validation before multipartbody.NewFile.","The Add buffering change expands scope and may impose large memory use on callers supplying custom multipart bodies.","Tests omit validation and source-reader error cases, although their multipart retry assertions are otherwise strong."],"risks_b":["It adds an unrelated public PersonsService.UploadPicture API and tests, violating scope discipline.","Upload tests do not assert uploaded content bytes, do not verify the multipart body on each retry attempt, and omit validation and source-reader failure cases.","The combined validation error is less specific than separate filename/content errors, though it satisfies the stated validation requirement."]}
